A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PersonaConflicts study. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original human annotations, backstory-effect and mediation analyses, and evaluations of three LLMs in Sections 5–7.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports individual human–model rating comparisons in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The simulation pipeline, NVC categories, backstory generation, and model inference procedures are unchanged. The full generation and evaluation prompts in Appendix A match.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 5,772-dialogue corpus, 120-conversation annotation subset, relationship categories, and problematicness/emotional-impact tasks. Appendix E illustrates retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains GPT-4o, Llama-4-Maverick, and Gemini-1.5-pro under the same context conditions. Newly cited datasets and studies are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The participant and annotation counts, context conditions, temperature-zero inference, label aggregation, and F1 evaluation remain unchanged. Appendix B newly documents annotation controls without establishing a revision to the existing protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix E adds five individual error examples across the three models, pairing backstories and utterances with human and model ratings. These supplement the retained quantitative bias analysis with concrete illustrations.

E5.justification: Agreement measures, t-tests, effect sizes, mediation estimates, Wilcoxon tests, and significance reporting are retained. No additional repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the quantitative figures retain their results. Appendix E adds individual ratings, including emotional-impact ratings of human 1.5 versus GPT-4o 3.0 and human 2.5 versus Gemini 1.0; these are newly reported examples, not aggregate performance changes.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. The NVC framework and reported mediation model remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, research questions, and conclusion retain the corpus contribution and claims about human sensitivity to backstory, LLM difficulties using it, and emotional-positivity bias.

C2.justification: The existing limitations are expanded to distinguish believability from representativeness, identify possible structure imposed by NVC-based generation, and specify English/Western and detection-only scope. v2 explicitly frames the corpus as a proof-of-concept testbed while retaining the main result interpretations.

D1.justification: The dataset footnote replaces a future-release promise with a repository access link. New Appendix B discloses Master's-status workers, attention checks, low-effort filtering, and minimum completion times; these are additional documentation of the existing study.

R1.justification: v2 adds NormDial, SocialDial, ToxiGen, and Unintended Offense citations to support validation and crowdworker practices. Section 4 also replaces the categorical absence-of-suitable-datasets statement with a privacy and collection-difficulty rationale.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify dataset motivation and validation, and reorganize limitations into three named topics. New appendix sections cover quality controls and error examples; the main section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 5–7 and appendix screenshots/tables are relocated, and Appendix E introduces boxed rating examples. All seven existing figures, four tables, and survey screenshots retain their content within the same overall two-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing study easier to assess and reuse through dataset access information, annotation-control documentation, clearer validity and applicability limits, and concrete error examples. These improve transparency and interpretation, while the underlying experimental evidence and central conclusions remain unchanged.
